title: yardstick label file, format 1.0.0
description: One subject's labels for one package type, at <subject>/<type>.json, where <subject> is pkg/oci/<registry>/<repository>/sha256-<hex>/ for an image or sbom/sha256-<hex>/ for an SBOM document, and <type> is the package type of the labels' packages. Two other kinds of file share this shape: <subject>/image.json holds labels that name no package, and global/<type>.json holds labels for every subject and has no subject. A label is one person's call on whether a scanner reporting one vulnerability on one package is right. Unknown fields are allowed, so an additive change never breaks an older reader; a label's own unknown fields survive a rewrite by an older yardstick, and unknown fields anywhere else do not. Justifications, fact sources, rules and vulnerability namespaces are not listed here: they are the corpus's vocabulary, in its vocabulary.yaml, and grow without a schema change.

schema.description: The version of this format the file is written in, as SchemaVer MODEL.REVISION.ADDITION. A reader reads any version of its own MODEL; the corpus's publish.yaml names the MODEL (format: v1 for 1.x.y).

subject.description: What the file's labels are about, which must be the subject its directory names. Required outside global/, and absent in global/ files.

labels.description: The labels, sorted by package then vulnerability (package-less first), with at most one label per package and vulnerability.

digest.description: A sha256 digest of some bytes, as sha256:<64 lowercase hex>.

subject.description: An image by digest, or an SBOM document by the digest of its bytes. Exactly one of image and sbom is set.

image.description: The image reference, pinned by digest: <registry>/<repository>[:tag]@sha256:<digest>.

sbom.description: The digest of the SBOM document's bytes, for a subject that is a document rather than an image. Its directory is sbom/sha256-<hex>/.

platform.description: The platform the image was cataloged for, as os/arch[/variant]. Required when image's digest is an index rather than a single manifest.

label.description: One call on one match: whether a scanner reporting vulnerability on package for this subject is right. A label is about the match, in CycloneDX's false_positive sense rather than VEX's not_affected.

package.description: The package as a purl. The label pairs a match when every field this purl states equals the match package's, so a field it leaves out, such as the version or a qualifier, matches anything. Required in type files and global/ files; a global label applies only on a subject whose SBOM has a package it matches. Absent in image.json, where the label pairs every match of its vulnerability on the subject whatever the package, and does not apply on a subject that filters its packages.

vulnerability.description: The vulnerability id. It pairs a match whose vulnerability shares an alias group with it, so a CVE label pairs a match reported under a GHSA that aliases it. Its namespace, the part before the first -, must be listed in vocabulary.yaml's vulnerability-namespaces or advisory-ids. An id in an advisory namespace (advisory-ids, such as ELSA or ALAS2) judges the match grype reported under exactly that id: it never joins an alias group, pairs no match reported under a CVE the advisory names, and on its own match decides over labels on those CVEs.

verdict.description: The call. tp: the match is right, the vulnerability affects the package. fp: the match is wrong. unclear: someone looked and could not decide; a match with only unclear labels scores as unlabeled.

justification.description: Why the verdict, as one of the values vocabulary.yaml lists under justifications.<verdict>. Required for fp and unclear, optional for tp.

author.description: The person who made the call. Whoever reviewed it is in the pull request that added it.

evidence.description: What the call rests on: each entry is one or more facts, the policy rule they satisfy if any, and what they mean for this call.

notes.description: What people said about the label and when, such as the conclusion tying the evidence together or what still needs checking. A migration writes notes on a person's behalf.

at.description: When it was said, as an RFC 3339 time.

seenIn.description: What the label was written against: the SBOM scanned and the tools that cataloged and matched it. Context for a reader judging whether the call is still current; pairing does not read it.

sbom.description: The digest of the SBOM the match was seen in.

tools.description: The tools, by name and version. yardstick records syft, grype and grype-db, with the DB's checksum as grype-db's version; labels from elsewhere may name other tools.

version.description: Its version, or for grype-db the DB's checksum.

firstIssued.description: When the call was first made, as an RFC 3339 time. Replacing a label keeps it. A published snapshot carries no git history, so a label carries its own dates.

lastUpdated.description: When the label last changed, as an RFC 3339 time.

evidence.description: One piece of evidence: the raw facts, the labeling policy rule they satisfy if any, and what they mean for this call.

rule.description: The labeling policy rule these facts satisfy, as a key of vocabulary.yaml's rules. The rule names the verdict it supports, which must be the label's unless the rule supports any.

facts.description: The raw observations, at least one.

interpretation.description: What the facts mean for this call, in plain words.
examples: Ubuntu fixed it in 245.4-4ubuntu3.2, and the installed 245.4-4ubuntu3.16 is later

fact.description: A raw observation someone can check again: in source, the record about these things had field set to value, when observed.

source.description: Where it was observed, as a value listed in vocabulary.yaml's fact-sources.

url.description: Where to look at it again, when the source has an address for it.

about.description: Which record in the source, as the key-value pairs that identify it there, such as vulnerability, package and release.

field.description: The field of that record that was read.

observedAt.description: When it was read, as an RFC 3339 time. Sources change, so a fact holds as of this time.
